summary: A hand-written subject-based publish/subscribe broker in TypeScript on node:net, zero runtime dependencies, wire-compatible with the core NATS client protocol. Stage 1: a streaming parser for CONNECT, PUB, SUB, UNSUB, PING and PONG that survives frames split at any byte, reads payloads by their declared byte count, rejects an over-long control line before its newline arrives and an over-size PUB before any payload is buffered; a SubjectTrie with * and > wildcards that prunes empty branches; a Broker with INFO, verbose (+OK), echo, at-most-once fan-out as MSG, auto-unsubscribe via UNSUB <sid> <max>, server PINGs that drop a client with -ERR 'Stale Connection' after maxPingsOut unanswered PINGs, fatal vs non-fatal -ERR, and stats. Stage 2: queue groups (each message goes to ONE member per group, picked with Math.random; plain subscribers still get every message); headers (HPUB in, HMSG out, header block must start with NATS/1.0, headers count against max_payload, and a client that did not ask for headers gets the body only as a plain MSG); 'no responders' (a request that reaches nobody gets an immediate HMSG with status 503 on the requester's inbox, only if it sent headers:true and no_responders:true); slow-consumer protection (a per-client maxPending cap on socket.writableLength, default 64 MiB; over it the client is counted, sent -ERR 'Slow Consumer' and its socket destroyed at once, so it usually never sees the -ERR); graceful close(forceMs) that ends every socket so queued bytes flush and destroys only after forceMs. Stage 3: a full-mesh cluster over our OWN route protocol (RINFO, RS+, RS-, RMSG with JSON meta; inspired by NATS routes but NOT compatible with them): counted interest propagation (announce on 0 -> 1, withdraw on 1 -> 0, disconnect counts, full sync on handshake), one-hop forwarding (a message from a route is never sent to another route, so a full mesh has no loops or duplicates), cluster-wide queue groups (the origin broker picks a local member if it has one, otherwise exactly one peer, and the RMSG lists the groups that peer must serve), a symmetric duplicate-connection rule (keep the route dialled by the smaller server id), self-route detection, re-dial with exponential backoff, and client failover with the official client. Framing is shared by both protocols in src/framer.ts. The CLI refuses a non-loopback bind (client or cluster port) unless ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1 because there is no authentication. 138 tests, incl. interop with the official nats npm client (2.29.3). 12 stage-1, 11 stage-2 and 11 stage-3 deliberate mutations were run; 33 were caught by a test and one (C7, receiver ignoring the 'plain' flag) is documented as not catchable. NOT done: authentication (clients and routes), TLS, persistence, a max-connections limit, route PING/PONG and a slow-route limit, anything but a full mesh (no gossip of peer addresses), requiring CONNECT before other operations, and a batching write path (throughput is about 12x below nats-server, see stage 4). Stage 4: measured on three real servers (two ARM, one x86) over a private network with raw JSON results, median of 3 runs with min-max, CPU steal recorded (1.07%) and README tables generated from the raw files: B1 fan-out about 37k-48k delivered msg/s on one broker; B2 the same raw-protocol bench client against nats-server v2.15.3 gave about 12x more, and p99 request/reply 1037 us vs 315 us; B3 one route hop round trip p50 1315 us vs 224 us local; B4 SIGKILL of the subscriber's broker at 2000 msg/s lost 20-29 messages, no duplicates, client reconnect about 8-10 ms; B5 slow consumer dropped at every limit but broker memory grew 2.6-4.6x the limit and was not given back (open question); B6 queue group about 25% per remote member and 1000/0 local preference; B7 a 10-minute churn left 0 connections, subscriptions and remote interest (cannot rule out a slow memory leak). Two bench bugs were found and fixed (a paused socket never sees close; nats-server's ready line on stderr plus an unhandled rejection crashed the first run). Deployment used temporary /32 security-list and iptables rules, before/after snapshots, and the diff found an orphaned nats-server. Messages published before an RS+ arrives, and messages in flight when a broker dies, are lost (at most once).

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek NATS jaisa message broker khud likha hai, TypeScript mein, sirf node:net par, koi runtime dependency nahi. Client subject par publish karta hai jaise orders.eu.created, aur us waqt ke matching subscribers (wildcards * aur > ke saath) ko message milta hai -- at-most-once, kuch store nahi hota. Queue groups se workers kaam baant lete hain, headers aur 'no responders' bhi hain, aur jo subscriber padhna band kar de use slow consumer bana ke kaat diya jaata hai taaki server ki memory na bhare. Teen ya zyada brokers ek full-mesh cluster bana sakte hain apne route protocol par, jahan message sirf usi broker ko jaata hai jiske clients ko interest hai. Official nats client bina change ke isse chalta hai, aur broker marne par doosre broker par failover karta hai. 138 tests, aur 34 rules jaan-boojh ke tode: 33 pakde gaye, aur ek (C7) ke baare mein likha hai ki woh kyun pakda nahi ja sakta.
pitch.explain_2min:
Yeh H12 hai: core NATS ka chhota version, chaar stages done (teesra cluster, chautha real servers par measurement). H5 (mini Kafka) log tha; yeh ulta hai: message usi pal ke subscribers ko jaata hai aur phir khatam.

src/framer.ts: TCP byte stream hai, toh Framer state rakhta hai, control line newline tak padhta hai aur payload declared byte count se. src/parser.ts (client protocol) aur src/route.ts (route protocol) sirf lines ka matlab tay karte hain aur payload ho toh framer.expect(n) bulate hain. Limits padhte waqt lagti hain: lambi control line newline se pehle reject, bada payload ek bhi byte buffer karne se pehle reject.

src/subjects.ts: SubjectTrie, subscription tokens se store, match mein literal, * aur > branches, remove par pruning.

src/server.ts: Broker. INFO, CONNECT se verbose, echo, headers, no_responders. publish trie.match karta hai: plain subscriptions ko har ek ko copy, aur har queue group ko ek copy ek random member ko. deliver() ek frame banata hai -- MSG ya HMSG; jo client headers nahi maangta use sirf body milti hai. Frame likhne se pehle check: socket.writableLength + frame > maxPending toh woh slow consumer hai -- count, -ERR, aur socket turant destroy. Request ko koi na sune aur requester ne opt in kiya ho toh turant 503.

Liveness PING/PONG se, fatal vs non-fatal errors alag, aur close(forceMs) graceful: end() se queued bytes flush, forceMs ke baad hi destroy.

Cluster: har broker ek doosra port kholta hai. Brokers RINFO se pehchaan karte hain, RS+/RS- se batate hain ki unke clients kya sunte hain (sirf 0 -> 1 aur 1 -> 0 par), aur RMSG se message bhejte hain sirf un peers ko jinke paas interest hai. Route se aaya message kabhi aage nahi jaata -- full mesh mein yahi loops aur duplicates rokta hai. Queue group ka faisla origin broker karta hai: local member ho toh wahi, warna exactly ek peer.

Verification: framer test har byte offset par stream todta hai, raw TCP integration tests, 3 brokers ek process mein cluster tests, aur official nats client ke interop aur failover tests. Stage 4 mein teen real servers par measure kiya: same bench client se nats-server lagbhag 12 guna tez, broker kill par 20-29 messages ka loss, aur slow consumer par memory limit ki 2.6-4.6 guna -- ek open question. Honest limits: auth, TLS, persistence, max connections, route ping nahi hain.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek PUB ka safar, code ke order mein.

Broker.accept: setNoDelay(true), naya Client (apna Parser), INFO JSON (headers true, max_payload, client_id), aur unref kiya hua ping timer.

socket 'data' -> parser.feed -> framer.feed. Framer.drain: expect() se payload size set ho toh partsLen >= size + 2 tak wait (koi concat nahi), phir CRLF check, payload copy, onPayload. Warna LF dhoondo; buffer maxControlLine se bada aur LF nahi toh error; line mili toh onLine. Parser ka handleLine command samajhta hai; PUB/HPUB par pending set karke framer.expect(size); handlePayload mein HPUB ka header block NATS/1.0 se shuru hona chahiye. HPUB line par headerLen <= total aur headerLen >= 8, aur total > maxPayload toh reject -- headers bhi limit mein gine jaate hain. PUB aur HPUB dono ek hi Op 'PUB' bante hain, headerLen ke saath ya bina.

ParseError -> fatal: -ERR, socket.end(), drop(c, false) se subscriptions turant hatao, 2 s ka destroy timer.

handle CONNECT: verbose === true, echo !== false, headers === true, no_responders === true. SUB: invalid subject ya queue name (whitespace, dot, *, > nahi) par non-fatal -ERR; repeated sid ignore; Subscription {client, sid, subject, queue, max, delivered} client.subs aur trie dono mein.

publish: subject/reply valid, counters. trie.match ki copy par loop: echo false wala apna client skip; queue undefined toh seedha deliver, warna groups Map mein. Phir har group se Math.random se ek member. deliver: target closed toh false. headers wale target ko HMSG <subject> <sid> [reply] <hdr> <total>, baaki ko MSG sirf body ke saath (payload.subarray(headerLen)). Ek Buffer.concat, ek write. Usse pehle writableLength + frame.length > maxPending toh slowConsumer: counter, -ERR, drop with destroy. Phir delivered++ aur auto-unsubscribe. Agar kisi ko deliver nahi hua, reply hai, aur publisher ne headers aur no_responders dono maange, toh sendNoResponders: requester ki apni matching subscription dhoondh kar HMSG with 'NATS/1.0 503'.

close(forceMs): server.close, sab clients drop(false), har socket end() -- queued bytes pehle jaate hain, phir FIN -- aur sab close hon toh 'closed', forceMs paar toh destroy aur 'forced'.

Cluster (stage 3): publish local delivery ke baad har route ke interest trie se dekhta hai kaun plain chahta hai aur kis peer ke paas kaunse queue groups ke members hain. Local member wale group peers ko nahi jaate; baaki har group ke liye ek random peer. Har peer ko zyada se zyada ek RMSG {s, r, p, q, h}. Receiver fromRoute mein sirf local deliver karta hai: p true ho toh plain subscribers, aur sirf q mein likhe groups ka ek member -- aur kabhi kisi route ko aage nahi. Interest counted hai (localInterest map), handshake par poori list RS+ se jaati hai, aur duplicate connections ka faisla dono taraf ek hi rule se (chhota server id jis connection ka dialer hai woh bachta hai).

Hardest decisions: at-most-once; slow consumer par turant destroy (flush ka intezaar wahi memory hai jo wapas chahiye, isliye client -ERR aksar nahi dekhta); bytesWritten nahi, writableLength (jo abhi queued hai) -- ek mutation ne yeh fark saabit kiya; 503 sirf opt-in par kyunki purane clients HMSG nahi samjhte. Cluster mein: apna route protocol (NATS compatible nahi), one-hop forwarding jo sirf full mesh mein sahi hai, aur C7 mutation ko honestly 'not caught' likhna. Kami: auth nahi, route ping aur slow-route limit nahi, RS+ pahunchne se pehle ke messages aur in-flight messages jaate hain.

Stage 4 (measurement): teen real servers, raw JSON, median of 3 with min-max, CPU steal (1.07%), README tables generated. Same raw-protocol bench client se nats-server lagbhag 12x zyada delivered msg/s (36916 vs 428378 ek subscriber par) -- ek event loop aur per-delivery write/copy ki keemat; p50 latency paas (238 vs 194 us) lekin p99 1037 vs 315 us. B4 mein subscriber ke broker ka SIGKILL: 20-29 messages ek contiguous block mein gaye, zero duplicates, client 8-10 ms mein reconnect. B5: slow consumer har limit par kata, lekin RSS limit ki 2.6-4.6 guna badha aur wapas nahi aaya -- open question. B6: har remote member ko lagbhag 25%, local member hone par 1000/0. B7: 10 minute churn ke baad 0 state (slow memory leak rule out nahi). Do bench bugs (paused socket kabhi close nahi dekhta; nats-server ka ready line stderr par + unhandled rejection) aur deployment hygiene (/32 rules, iptables top par, setsid/ssh -n, pkill '[h]12', snapshot diff jisne orphaned nats-server pakda).
pitch.architecture_walkthrough:
src/framer.ts: ParseError, Framer (feed, drain, flatten, keep, expect, buffered) -- byte stream se lines aur byte-counted payloads; dono protocols share karte hain.

src/parser.ts: client protocol: Op type (PUB with headerLen), ParserLimits, Parser (feed, handleLine incl. HPUB, handlePayload, buffered), parseCount, HEADER_PREFIX. Socket ke bina test hota hai.

src/route.ts: route protocol: RouteOp, RouteMsgMeta, RouteParser (RINFO, RS+, RS-, RMSG, PING, PONG), validMeta, encodeRinfo, encodeInterest, encodeRmsg.

src/subjects.ts: tokenize, isValidSubscribeSubject, isValidPublishSubject, SubjectTrie (insert, remove with pruning, match via walk, size, nodeCount).

src/server.ts: BrokerOptions (host, port, serverName, maxPayload, maxControlLine, pingIntervalMs, maxPingsOut, maxPending, cluster), ClusterOptions (host, port, routes, reconnectMs), BrokerStats (incl. slowConsumers, routes, routeInMsgs, routeOutMsgs), Subscription, Client, Route (peerId, interest trie, dialedBySelf, url), Dialer (attempts, timer, peerId, self), Broker (listen, addRoute, close(forceMs), stats, routePeers, hasRemoteInterest, peerInterest, accept, pingTick, fatal, slowConsumer, drop, handle, subscribe, unsubscribe, removeSub, publish, fromRoute, deliver, sendNoResponders, interestUp, interestDown, dial, scheduleDial, setupRoute, handleRoute, handshake, routeGone).

src/index.ts: env config (HOST, PORT, MAX_PAYLOAD, PING_INTERVAL_MS, MAX_PINGS_OUT, MAX_PENDING, CLUSTER_PORT, CLUSTER_HOST, ROUTES, ROUTE_RECONNECT_MS), client aur cluster dono hosts par non-loopback refusal bina ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK=1, SIGINT/SIGTERM par stats log, graceful close, 'stopped' log with closed/forced.

test/: helpers.ts (startBroker, Raw hand-driven client, until), parser, subjects, server, stage2 (queue groups, headers, no responders, slow consumer, graceful close), route.test.ts (route protocol encode/parse), cluster.test.ts (startNode, startCluster: 3 brokers on ephemeral ports in one process; mesh, interest, queue groups, restart, failover), interop.test.ts (official nats client). 138 tests in total.
difficult_decisions: Payload ko byte count se padhna, CRLF dhoond kar nahi: binary aur CRLF wale payloads sahi chalte hain.
Limits ko buffer karne se PEHLE lagana; HPUB mein headers bhi max_payload mein gine jaate hain.
Fatal vs non-fatal errors: framing toot gayi toh connection band, galat subject ya queue name par sirf -ERR.
Slow consumer par socket turant destroy, end() nahi: flush ka intezaar wahi memory hai jo wapas leni hai; keemat yeh ki client -ERR aksar nahi dekhta.
Slow-consumer check socket.writableLength (abhi queued bytes) par, bytesWritten (ab tak ka total) par nahi.
503 no-responders sirf tab jab client ne headers aur no_responders dono maange; warna HMSG purane clients ko tod deta.
At-most-once aur zero persistence: H5 durability sikhata hai, yahan routing, fan-out aur back-pressure focus hai.
Apna route protocol, NATS routes ke saath compatible nahi: chhota, test karne layak, aur claim karne mein honest.
One-hop forwarding: route se aaya message kabhi aage nahi -- full mesh mein loop-free aur duplicate-free, lekin har broker ko har broker tak pahunchna zaroori.
Queue group ka faisla sirf origin broker karta hai (local pehle, warna ek peer), taaki poore cluster mein ek hi member ko mile.
Measurement ke liye apna raw-protocol bench client, aur wahi client real nats-server ke against -- taaki pata chale bottleneck broker hai ya generator.
README tables haath se nahi, raw JSON se generate; weak columns (B4 'first message again') aur open questions (B5 memory) bhi likhe.
biggest_challenges: TCP split frames: test stream ko har single offset par aur byte-by-byte todta hai, ab HPUB ke saath bhi.
Fatal error par -ERR pahunchana aur socket half-open na chhodna: end(), drop(false), 2 s destroy timer.
Slow consumer ka test: subscriber ka socket.pause() karke kernel aur server buffers bharne dena, aur saath mein dikhana ki tez subscriber maxPending se kahin zyada total bhejne par bhi nahi katta.
Graceful close ko saabit karna: 500 messages queued, close() 'closed' de aur subscriber ko sab 500 milein; aur ek half-open peer ke saath 'forced'.
Queue group test random pick ke saath deterministic rakhna: dono members ko kuch mila, total exact, plain subscriber ko sab.
Duplicate connections: dono brokers ek doosre ko dial karte hain; ek symmetric rule chahiye tha jisse dono ek hi connection band karein (C4 mutation ne 12 tests tode).
C7 mutation kisi test se nahi pakda gaya, aur analysis ne dikhaya ki in tests se pakda ja hi nahi sakta; ise README mein 'not caught' likha, chhupaya nahi.
Distributed readiness: probe subjects asli SUB ke baad bhejna, aur route ordering se saabit karna ki asli interest bhi pahunch gayi.
Do bench bugs: paused socket ko close ka intezaar (broker counter se fix) aur nats-server ke stderr ready line ke saath un-awaited promise ka crash.
failure_scenarios: Slow consumer: maxPending paar hote hi woh client kat jaata hai aur uske queued messages jaate hain; baaki clients chalte rehte hain.
Server restart ya crash: sab subscriptions memory mein thi, in-flight messages kho jaate hain; at-most-once mein yeh expected hai.
Half-open TCP: server PING aur maxPingsOut ise pakadte hain; shutdown par forceMs ke baad destroy.
Galat byte count ya galat header block: fatal -ERR aur connection band, doosre clients par asar nahi.
Bahut saare connections: max connections limit nahi hai, aur har client ka maxPending alag hai, toh total memory ki koi upper bound nahi.
Cluster mein broker marna: uske clients failover karke doosre broker par jaate hain aur dobara subscribe karte hain, lekin us beech aur route par in-flight messages jaate hain.
Naya subscriber: uska RS+ publisher ke broker tak pahunchne se pehle publish hue messages forward nahi hote.
Route jo jawab dena band kare: route ki apni PING/PONG nahi hai (sirf TCP keepalive) aur slow-route limit nahi.
Measured (B5): bada maxPending (512 MiB) 1 GB machine ko maar deta, kyunki RSS limit ki 2.6-4.6 guna badhta hai.
improvements: Token auth (clients aur routes dono), per-subject permissions, phir TLS.
Route PING/PONG aur slow-route limit (maxPending jaisa).
Full mesh se aage: peer addresses ka gossip, ya multi-hop ke liye loop prevention.
Max connections aur total pending memory limit; CONNECT ko pehla op hona enforce karna.
Metrics export (slowConsumers, per-client pending) aur alerts.
Throughput gap (lagbhag 12x) par kaam: per-connection batching (cork/writev), kam copies, aur har change ke baad wahi bench.
B5 memory finding ki jaanch: heap snapshots aur allocator behaviour, aur lamba soak taaki slow leak rule out ho.
